title: The 1922 Modern Art Week: Which Se?

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know the different jobs of *se* from B2 Unit 19: reflexive, reciprocal, passive, impersonal and accidental. A text about an art movement uses several of them in a few lines, so it is a good place to ask "who does what to whom?" Here they work on the Modern Art Week of 1922.

sections.title: Five kinds of se, in São Paulo, 1922
rows: Reflexive: someone does it to themselves
Los jóvenes artistas se presentaron ante el público. (presented themselves)
Reciprocal: two or more do it to each other
Los modernistas se conocían y se escribían cartas. (wrote to each other)
Passive: a thing, no doer named
En 1922 se celebró la Semana de Arte Moderna. (was held)
Se dice que el público abucheó a los artistas. (it is said)
Accidental: se + me, te, le, nos
Se me perdió el programa de la exposición. (I lost the programme)

items.spanish: Se leyeron poemas y se presentaron cuadros durante tres noches.
items.english: Poems were read and paintings were shown over three nights.

items.spanish: Oswald y Tarsila se admiraban mucho.
items.english: Oswald and Tarsila admired each other a lot.

items.spanish: Se nos olvidó el catálogo en casa.
items.english: We forgot the catalogue at home.

sections.content: Ask what the noun does. If *se* + a plural thing agrees with the verb (*se leyeron poemas*), it is passive. If nobody is named and there is no noun (*se dice que*), it is impersonal. If *me, te, le, nos* follows *se* and the verb agrees with the thing (*se me perdió el programa*), it is accidental.
